note: No AI features, so no ai_* labels. Public Next.js directory (static export) plus a Vite admin console on Supabase. Env examples are empty. Admin pages check the session only in browser code, and the real gate is the database policies, which let any signed-in user write.

labels.what: stores_auth_write and store_tags_auth_write let ANY authenticated user insert, update and delete every row (using true, with check true). There is no admin role or allowlist. Same pattern in cuisines and areas migrations (policies cuisines_auth_write, areas_auth_write)

Auth signups are enabled (also line 99 for SMS) and email confirmations are off. Combined with the write policy, anyone can sign up and edit or delete the whole directory. The migration comment only says to turn signups off in the dashboard by hand
Any authenticated user can upload to or delete from the public store-logos bucket (folder stores only). No admin check
The browser deletes stores directly with the anon-key client (also StoreForm.tsx line 278 for tags). Safe only if the policies were tight, and they are not
The admin dashboard is shown or hidden by a browser session check only. This is fine as UI, but there is no role check beyond being signed in
Supabase URL and anon key read from VITE_ env vars in browser code (also web/lib/supabase.ts lines 7-8). The anon key is public by design. No secret value present

10 hardcoded stores used when Supabase env vars are missing. The data layer falls back silently, so a misconfigured build ships sample stores as real (web/lib/data.ts lines 56-60). Real brands with real links, so the data is not fake
Seed migration that duplicates web/data/seed.ts as a second copy of the same 10 stores
Site URL falls back to https://sg-remote-food-order.example.com for canonical links and sitemap
Region list (central, north, north-east, east, west) fixed in a CHECK constraint and again in web/data/regions.ts
